abstract.para: /etc/sysconfig/kdump is the main &kdump; configuration file. Every option is documented with comments directly in the file. This table summarizes the ones you need most often.

row.entry: Crash kernel memory reservation. auto (default) uses the value from kdumptool calibrate. See .

When true (default), kdump-commandline.service updates the boot loader configuration whenever the running kernel command line does not match the expected crashkernel= options. Set to false to only check and warn, without modifying the boot loader.
Kernel version string to use for the capture kernel. Leave empty to auto-detect a suitable kernel.
Number of CPUs available to the capture kernel environment (default: 32, or all available CPUs if set to 0). Lowering this reduces the capture kernel's memory footprint.
Where captured dumps are stored. Defaults to /var/crash. See for remote targets.
Number of old dumps to keep. Honored only for local save directories. The default, 0, never deletes old dumps. -1 deletes all old dumps, so that only the newly saved dump remains.
Minimum free space, in megabytes, that must remain at the save location after writing a dump. &kdump; refuses to save a dump that would drop below this threshold. Default: 64.
How much of memory to include in the dump, from 0 (largest, most complete dump) to 31 (smallest, the default). See man 5 kdump for the table of levels.

Format of the saved dump. The default, compressed, produces small dumps that only crash can analyze. ELF produces larger dumps that GDB can also read. none saves only the kernel log. See man 5 kdump for the other formats.
When true (default), the system reboots automatically once the dump is saved.
When true (default), the capture kernel continues with the next action after an error while saving or deleting dumps. Set to false to open a shell at that point instead. See .
Bit mask that sets the verbosity of the dump process (default: 0). See .

The complete command line for the capture kernel. By default, &kdump; builds it from the running system's command line. If you set it yourself, it must include the root parameter, any console parameters, irqpoll, and reset_devices. To only add options, use KDUMP_COMMANDLINE_APPEND instead.

Extra kernel command-line options to append for the capture kernel, for example networking-related parameters needed for a remote dump target. For network dumps, you may need net_delay=SECONDS to give the network device time to become operational. For example, net_delay=20 waits 20 seconds.
Path to the SSH private key used when KDUMP_SAVEDIR points at an ssh:// or sftp:// target. See .

important.title: Restart &kdump; after editing its configuration
important.para: After changing /etc/sysconfig/kdump, run systemctl restart kdump for the change to take effect. An exception is KDUMP_CRASHKERNEL: since it changes the boot-time memory reservation, it requires a full system reboot, not just a service restart, and on the immutable variant an additional explicit step. See .
